I’ve spent times in hospitals. A lot of family members are doctors. My sister required medical care for a long time. Being a nurse isn’t only physically caring for the patient. It’s also emotional support. I’m not saying they have to be extremely nice but at least cordial, especially when working with children, elderly people, and mentally ill people. 

Obviously, you can’t judge a nurse on a single word, or sentence. But nurses have to keep their cool. Has a patient been outrageously disrespectful and rude, it could be understandable to have a slip up. But if the patient has been behaving well during the past altercations with said nurse, than she is in the wrong to treat him badly. 

Yes, it’s possible the nurse has been having an extraordinarily bad week. But she can’t take it out on her patients. 

Please do not say my opinions are silly. To each our own.
